models_evaluated: In-house deep-learning 3D UNet thoracic OAR auto-segmentation models (9 single-organ models)

links.outcome: Correlation of standalone geometric metrics with clinician correction times
links.effect: Weak to negligible Spearman correlations between geometric metrics and correction times for most OARs; significant only for aorta, esophagus, left lung. Time savings could not be predicted from geometric metrics.
links.quote: Time saving potential could not be estimated from model geometric performance metrics.

links.outcome: Contouring time with AI-assisted correction versus manual contouring
links.effect: Median total contouring time reduced by 12.6 min (50.3%, p<0.01); significant for lungs and heart, but increases for left bronchial tree (+22.9%), esophagus (+10.3%), trachea (+20.8%).
links.quote: Statistically significant median time reductions – based on a p < 0 . 025 threshold – were observed for the right lung (5.7 min, a 90.7% reduction), left lung (5.9 min, a 92.7% reduction), heart (1.1 min, a 52.9% reduction) and total contouring time (12.6 min, a 50.3% reduction).

models_evaluated: In-house 3D UNet thoracic auto-segmentation models for nine organs-at-risk

links.outcome: Physician contouring time with auto-segmentation assistance versus manual contouring
links.effect: Median total contouring time was 750 s with assistance versus 1509 s manually, a 50.3% reduction (p-value <0.01). Interface use and model execution totaling approximately 3 min were excluded.
links.quote: Statistically significant median time reductions – based on a p < 0 . 025 threshold – were observed for the right lung (5.7 min, a 90.7% reduction), left lung (5.9 min, a 92.7% reduction), heart (1.1 min, a 52.9% reduction) and total contouring time (12.6 min, a 50.3% reduction).

links.outcome: Association between geometric segmentation metrics and physician correction time
links.effect: Correlations were weak to negligible for most organs. DSC–correction-time correlations included right lung −0.35 [0.36] and heart −0.15 [0.70], with p-values in brackets.
links.quote: The Spearman correlation coefficients and corresponding p-values reveal weak to negligible correlations of individual geometric metrics versus correction times for most organs.

links.outcome: Incomplete auto-generated organ contours identified during clinical correction
links.effect: Aorta and heart auto-segmentations contained missing slices in 5 cases, with one to three missing slices each.
links.quote: These anomalies were primarily due to missing slices in the auto-segmentations for these structures, which were present in 5 cases with one to three missing slices each and disproportionately impacted totalAPL.

links.effect: AI-assisted contouring reduced median total contouring time by 50.3% (12.6 min) compared to manual contouring.
links.quote: Median contouring times were reduced for six out of nine OARs leading to a reduction of 50.3 % or 12.6 min in median total contouring time.

links.outcome: correlation between geometric metrics and correction time
links.effect: Standalone geometric performance metrics showed weak to negligible correlations with the manual correction time required by clinicians.
links.quote: The Spearman correlation coefficients and corresponding p-values reveal weak to negligible correlations of individual geometric metrics versus correction times for most organs.
